newsitem.title: GERMANY: Delta agrees German job plan, hunger strike ends.
newsitem.headline: Delta agrees German job plan, hunger strike ends.

text.p: U.S. airline Delta Airlines has agreed compensation packages for the 440 German staff it is planning to lay off, union officials said on Friday.

Separately, the five Delta workers who had been protesting at the near halving of the airline's German workforce had called off their 11-day hunger strike outside its check-out counters at Frankfurt airport, they added.

Officials at the OeTV transport trade union said Delta had agreed to pay workers redundancy packages worth up to 250,000 marks ($149,000). The job cuts are linked to Delta's move to drop six European and three U.S. flights out of Frankfurt.

A further 160 workers are due to be taken on by the FAG Frankfurt airport operating company and negotiations are taking place for 60 Delta staff to be transferred to German flag-carrier Deutsche Lufthansa AG, the OeTV said.
Walk-outs by workers last month had caused delays to some Delta flights.
